title: Can Deterministic Network Verification Reduce Undetected Faults in LLM‑Generated Configurations?
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study id c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) to measure whether inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM intent→configuration generator and an emulated execution reduces the proportion of configurations that would execute with operational faults. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics (one identical LLM candidate per intent evaluated both without and with verification), we evaluated 72 preregistered paired intents with gpt-5-mini and a canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution completed with 144 episodes (72 pairs) and 72 model calls. All baseline executions produced no emulator-observed faults (n_11 = 72, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0). The paired difference in undetected-fault proportion is 0.0 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.0], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics this degenerate confirmatory outcome is expected when identical generated candidates produce no baseline execution faults. We present preregistration rationale, deterministic execution accounting, representative validator diagnostics, exact inferential outputs, and concrete artifact-supported recommendations for follow-on designs able to detect verifier utility under realistic baseline-error regimes.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intents into device-level configurations for network operations (NetOps). Intent→configuration translation promises to accelerate change pipelines but risks silently violating reachability, policy, ordering, or workflow invariants and causing outages if generated text is executed without further checks. A commonly proposed mitigation is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) architecture: stochastic LLM generation followed by deterministic verification and, when necessary, repair or human review. Existing work demonstrates promise for intent→config translation in constrained settings [1], and prototype co-pilots recommend integrated verification [2], yet systematic preregistered experiments that measure verifier detection performance against executed outcomes are scarce [3].

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment that isolates deterministic verifier detection on identical LLM outputs under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The research question is: does inserting a deterministic network verifier between an LLM generator and emulator execution materially reduce the proportion of configurations that execute with operational faults when the identical generated candidate is evaluated both without and with verification? The design intentionally isolates detection (verifier flagging) from improvements that could arise from alternate generator samples, prompt modifications, or repair-enabled iterations. Our principal contribution is an artifact-grounded, fully archived confirmatory run (72 paired intents) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, plus concrete, artifact-supported recommendations for experimental contracts able to reveal verifier utility when baseline error prevalence is non‑negligible.
sections.related_work:
Prior literature spans intent-based configuration generators, tool‑augmented agentic frameworks, and GVR architectural proposals. Nguyen et al. evaluated intent→configuration pipelines in emulator settings and reported task-level correctness in constrained vendor-dialect subsets [1]. Multi-agent and tool-augmented frameworks for intent-driven NetOps (e.g., Confucius-style systems) have been proposed and prototyped; these works frequently propose integrated verification to reduce regressions but typically omit preregistered detection-evaluations tied to emulator-executed outcomes [2].

Generate–Verify–Repair architectures have empirical precedent in software and code-generation domains where deterministic checkers and test suites validate stochastic outputs and drive repair iterations; these motivate similar pipelines for NetOps but do not provide extensive empirical coupling with network verifiers and emulated execution outcomes [3]. Constraint‑enforcing decoding and integer-programming constrained decoding reduce structured-output violations in evaluated domains and suggest complementary strategies for NetOps [4]. Classical deterministic network-verification methods (header-space/semantic policy checkers) provide precise invariants (reachability, ACL semantics, ordering) and are natural verifier candidates; however, prior literature lacks preregistered paired experiments that report verifier true/false detection rates against emulator failures for identical generated candidates [5].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001 and froze the design before observing outcomes. The primary estimand is the paired reduction in undetected operational-fault proportion (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). Confirmatory H1 targeted an absolute paired reduction of 0.20 (two-sided alpha = 0.05, power ≥ 0.80); power calculations gave ≈63 pairs required and we preregistered N = 72 pairs (24 per topology-difficulty stratum).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract. The execution_contract enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent exactly one initial LLM generation was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated in two conditions. Baseline: execute the shared candidate in an isolated emulator and record emulator fault/no-fault. Guarded: run the canonical deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on the same candidate; if the verifier flags violations the guarded outcome is recorded as prevented (no execution); if it does not flag, execute the identical candidate and record the emulation outcome. Under this contract the guarded arm can only change the executed outcome by preventing an otherwise executed fault.

Model and adapter settings. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (provider = openai_responses, max_output_tokens = 2000, maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The model configuration records temperature = null; that is, sampling parameters were left to provider default at runtime and are archived as residual sampling-parameter uncertainty. The adapter family is hosted_netops_gvr_v1. All hosted-model call events and their counts are recorded in provider-call audit artifacts.

Verifier and scoring. The canonical verifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = "5.0") and implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule set, returning a binary per-episode validity verdict plus structured validator_traces (parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validation_before/after states, violation_codes, difficulty metadata). The verifier's trace objects were archived per episode and used to classify per-task difficulty and to confirm verifier execution.

Task generation, contamination controls, and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Each manifest entry encodes: a natural-language intent, a structured required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, initial/expected final states, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard). Pre-registered exact-match contamination checks against public corpora were applied; analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match flags for confirmatory pairs. The confirmatory sample remained stratified per preregistration (24 pairs per stratum).

Execution protocol, retries, and deterministic accounting. The missingness_plan allowed up to two retries for transient hosted-API errors (3 attempts total) for generation calls; all retries, timestamps, and provider-call events were logged. The run started at 2026-08-31T06:56:23.065707Z and completed at 2026-08-31T07:06:28.665518Z (≈10.1 minutes wall-clock). The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, failed_episode_count = 0, and model_calls_used = 72. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 72, cache_miss_count = 72, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 72}.

Analysis and inferential procedures. Each episode produced a binary indicator: emulator failure when executing the generated config (baseline_undetected = 1 if emulator failed) and guarded_undetected = 1 if verifier did not flag and emulator failed. The primary test used paired_binary_analysis_v1 to build the 2×2 contingency (guarded × baseline) and applied an exact McNemar two-sided test if discordant pairs existed. We computed paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CIs for the paired difference with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) as recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. Pre-specified subgroup comparisons (topology complexity, policy type) were registered with Holm correction.
sections.results:
Execution and manifest summary. The autonomous pipeline completed without technical failures. Key manifest figures: planned_episode_count = 144; completed_episode_count = 144; failed_episode_count = 0; model_calls_used = 72; artifact_count = 510. analysis/condition_summary.csv records baseline successes = 72, baseline failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded successes = 72, guarded failures = 0 (success_rate = 1.0).

Paired contingency and exact inference. Aggregating the 72 confirmatory pairs produced contingency counts n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0 (guarded × baseline). The paired estimate paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) is [0.0, 0.0], reflecting the degenerate distribution resulting from zero discordant pairs. analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain these tabulations.

Representative validator diagnostics. Per-episode scoring artifacts (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show parsed_command_count between 2 and 6, required_command_count matching parsed counts for valid sequences, difficulty.level spanning medium/hard/very_hard, normalized_configuration matching the shared candidate, validator_version = "5.0", score_reason_code = "VALID_CONFIGURATION", and violation_count = 0. For example, pair-000001 (task-000001) required a 4-step sequence (shutdown, mtu, vlan, restore) and the shared candidate matched the required_sequence exactly; the validator reported valid = true and violation_count = 0 in both pre/post traces.

Contamination, missingness, and sensitivity diagnostics. analysis/contamination_summary.csv reports zero exact-match contaminations for confirmatory pairs. analysis/missingness_summary.csv records complete_pairs = 72 and zero failed or unscorable episodes. Pre-specified sensitivity analyses (treating excluded confirmatory pairs as failures; bootstrap diagnostics) were executed and archived; because no pairs were excluded and no discordant outcomes occurred these sensitivity analyses reproduce the degenerate numeric conclusion (paired difference = 0.0).

Accounting and reproducibility checks. Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm episode accounting: planned_episode_count = 144, completed_episode_count = 144, complete_pair_count = 72, n_11 = 72, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0, and all deterministic consistency checks passed (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Provider-call audit entries record hosted_model_call_event_count = 72 and cache_miss_count = 72, consistent with one shared initial generation per pair.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory interpretation. The preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics validly measures verifier detection on identical candidates. Observing zero baseline faults yields a scientifically informative ceiling/null outcome: given the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), prompt/templates, and synthetic task bank the generator outputs were uniformly valid in the emulator; therefore the verifier had no executed failures to prevent. The numerical outputs (n_11 = 72; paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; bootstrap CI [0.0,0.0]) are direct consequences of the preregistered contract and observed data and therefore correctly reported as a degenerate confirmatory result.

Artifact-grounded causes of the ceiling outcome. Measurable factors that contributed include: (1) the deterministic task generator produced constrained, explicit required_sequence fields and allowed_touched_fields, increasing unambiguity; (2) gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json) produced sequences that matched those constraints across the synthetic corpus; and (3) the verifier rule set (full_intent_constraint_validation in deterministic_netops_validator_v5) aligns closely with the required_sequence constraints present in the task manifests, producing no violation flags. These artifact-supported factors together explain why baseline emulator executions produced no faults for the selected corpus.

Design recommendations for detecting verifier utility. To empirically measure practical verifier benefits we recommend preregistered designs that raise baseline error prevalence or permit verifier-mediated candidate changes. Artifact-grounded, preregistration-compatible alternatives include: (A) independent-generation arms—allow separate initial generations per condition so verifier-triggered repairs or alternative sampling may change executed candidate distributions; (B) repair-enabled flows—permit a deterministic repair call when the verifier flags violations and execute repaired candidates to measure end-to-end improvement; (C) adversarial/fault-injection task banks—seed tasks with ambiguous intents, ordering subtleties, or protocol edge cases to elevate baseline error prevalence; and (D) multi-model and explicit-sampling sweeps—include multiple model versions and fixed non-null temperatures to quantify model- and sampling-sensitivity. All options are implementable within the archived adapter and artifact-recording infrastructure and should be preregistered with clear estimands.

Threats to validity and operational implications. Internal validity: the shared_initial_candidate design isolates detection but prevents verifier-mediated candidate-selection effects; this tradeoff is by design. Construct validity: emulator-observed faults are a conservative proxy for operational harm but omit timing- and traffic-dependent device behaviors in production. External validity: the experiment used a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), a synthetic task bank, and one deterministic verifier; extrapolation beyond these settings is limited. Conclusion validity: because baseline error prevalence was zero in this corpus the confirmatory design had no power to detect verifier benefit here. Operationally, the ceiling outcome does not imply verifiers are unnecessary—rather, it demonstrates that under tightly constrained synthetic tasks an LLM alone can produce valid sequences; measuring verifier benefit in realistic operations requires tasks and sampling that produce non-negligible baseline faults.

Practical reproducibility guidance. Key artifacts required to reproduce the analysis are archived in the evidence bundle: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl, deterministic_reconciliation.json, and per-episode validator traces under execution/scoring/. The analysis bootstrap used seed = 1729 and 10,000 resamples; these values are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. The run-level timing, provider-call audit, and artifact counts are recorded in execution/ manifests to enable deterministic reconciliation of the paired accounting.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation (c1-gnr-vv-2026-0001) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure whether a canonical deterministic verifier reduces the proportion of LLM-generated configurations that would execute with operational faults. For the chosen model (gpt-5-mini), verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and synthetic/emulated task bank, baseline executions produced zero emulator faults and the verifier did not change outcomes (paired difference = 0.0; bootstrap 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; exact McNemar p = 1.0). This artifact-grounded null/ceiling outcome is internally consistent with the preregistered design: when identical generated candidates produce no executed faults a verifier cannot reduce executed faults under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Measuring verifier utility under realistic error regimes requires experimental contracts that permit independent or multiple generator samples, repair-enabled flows, adversarial task sets, and multi-model comparisons. The archived artifacts provide a reproducible baseline and a template for those follow-on confirmatory designs.

limitations: Confirmatory ceiling/null outcome: baseline generator produced zero emulator faults on the preregistered task set, preventing direct measurement of verifier detection benefit.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design measures verifier effect on the same generated candidate only and does not assess independent per‑condition generation, multi‑sample generation, or repairs unless explicitly permitted by the contract.
Single‑model scope: experiments used one declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply generality across models or versions.
Synthetic/emulated tasks: task corpus and emulator executions differ from production devices and live traffic; external validity to production deployments is limited.

Sampling‑parameter uncertainty: execution/model_configuration.json shows temperature = null (sampling parameters unset); null indicates provider default sampling semantics determined runtime sampling behavior and is a residual uncertainty recorded in the archived configuration.

Residual contamination risk: deterministic provenance and exact‑match checks were applied, but private training‑data contamination of the hosted model cannot be fully ruled out and remains residual uncertainty.
